<h1>Md Bodrud-Doza, PhD</h1>
<p class="appointment">Environmental and geospatial scientist</p>
<p class="affiliation"><a href="https://geg.uoguelph.ca/">Department of Geography, Environment and Geomatics</a> · <a href="https://www.uoguelph.ca/">University of Guelph</a>, Ontario, Canada</p>
<p class="hero-intro">Clean water, sustainable landscapes and resilient food systems depend on the same thing: good decisions about how land is managed. My research builds the evidence for those decisions.</p>
<p>I am a geographer who builds watershed models, maps and machine-learning tools that show conservation agencies where limited budgets will do the most good. Before my PhD I spent six years designing and managing climate-adaptation programs in Bangladesh. That is why my science starts from a practical test: will this work on a real farm, for the people who have to carry it out?</p>

## Decision science, from problem to solution {#problem-to-solution}

<figure class="field-banner"><img src="assets/images/research/field-monitoring-site.webp" width="1600" height="960" loading="lazy" alt="Aerial view of a stream flowing through a culvert between cropland, with a small monitoring station on the bank"><figcaption>Where the research starts: a monitored stream running between cropland. What leaves these fields in a storm ends up downstream.</figcaption></figure>

<ol class="pitch"><li><p class="eyebrow">The problem</p><h3>Nutrients lost from farmland feed algal blooms</h3><p>Conservation practices such as cover crops, buffers and drainage-water management reduce those losses, but only when they are put in the right place.</p></li><li><p class="eyebrow">What I do</p><h3>Rank fields and practices with models and data</h3><p>I combine monitoring records, process-based watershed models and machine learning, then adjust the ranking with what local farmers and conservation staff know.</p></li><li><p class="eyebrow">Why it matters</p><h3>Funding goes where it achieves most</h3><p>Agencies can direct stewardship budgets to the fields that count and explain that choice to the producers they work with.</p></li></ol>

## Research program

Three connected pillars make up the program I am developing, the [REAL Decision Lab](research.qmd). The first is established and published; the third is where the work is heading.

<div class="cards three pillars"><article class="research-card"><p class="status-label">Established foundation</p><h3>Precision conservation and agricultural watershed science</h3><p>Nutrient transport, tile drainage, conservation-practice evaluation and field-scale targeting, informed by local priorities.</p></article><article class="research-card"><p class="status-label">Established methods · emerging applications</p><h3>Environmental intelligence: GIS, Earth observation and GeoAI</h3><p>Spatial analysis and machine learning are established parts of my work. Satellite observation and GeoAI are directions I am building.</p></article><article class="research-card"><p class="status-label">Developing direction</p><h3>Resilient agricultural landscapes and adaptive decision support</h3><p>Multi-benefit conservation, climate adaptation and decision tools that are updated as monitoring shows what worked.</p></article></div>

<p class="section-link"><a href="research.qmd#research-pillars">How the pillars connect, and the five-year plan →</a></p>

## From field practice to predictive science {#career-path}

I did not come to watershed modelling by the usual route. I trained as an environmental scientist, worked for six years where climate decisions are made and paid for, and then returned to research to build better evidence for those decisions.

<ol class="career-path"><li><span class="path-years">2010–2014</span><strong>Environmental sciences</strong><span>BSc and MSc, Jahangirnagar University. Groundwater quality, GIS and geostatistics.</span></li><li><span class="path-years">2016–2018</span><strong>Adaptation research</strong><span>Research Officer, ICCCAD. Climate-adaptation and policy research.</span></li><li><span class="path-years">2018–2022</span><strong>Program leadership</strong><span>BRAC and ICCCAD. Climate-resilience programs, partnerships and proposals.</span></li><li><span class="path-years">2022–2026</span><strong>PhD in Geography</strong><span>University of Guelph. Precision conservation in tile-drained watersheds.</span></li><li class="path-now"><span class="path-years">2026–present</span><strong>Postdoctoral Scholar</strong><span>University of Guelph. Healthy Lake Huron monitoring, modelling and decision support.</span></li></ol>
